# Migration Requirements Checklist: .NET 10 Upgrade

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, clarity, and completeness of the .NET 10 upgrade requirements before task decomposition
**Created**: 2026-09-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are exact target versions specified for every pin surface (SDK, TFMs, WindowsAppSDK, Extensions, images, CI)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are requirements defined for recording the WindowsAppSDK spike outcome before client work begins? [Completeness, Research §R-03]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are fallback-version requirements specified when a keep-policy package fails (MVVM 8.4.2, newer 2.x re-check)? [Completeness, Research §R-03/R-05]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are existing performance-gate tests referenced as must-stay-green through the migration? [Completeness, Plan §Technical Context]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 - Is "warnings MUST NOT increase" quantified with a defined baseline artifact and comparison method? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is the WindowsAppSDK version resolved to an exact number (2.4.0) consistently across spec, plan, and research? [Clarity, Research §R-03]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is "no user-visible behavior change" scoped to an explicit screen/action list? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are the criteria for "package fails, therefore bump" explicitly defined (restore failure vs. build failure vs. warning)? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 - Do SDK/TFM/package/image/CI version requirements align across spec, plan, research, and the data-model audit list? [Consistency, Data Model §audit list]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the minimum-OS requirement consistent between FR-004, the unchanged 17763 TFM, and the 2.x back-compat claim? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK011 - Are test-suite references consistent (228-unit baseline, contract, offline suites) across spec SC-002 and plan testing context? [Consistency, Spec §SC-002]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 - Can SC-004 "zero references to the old runtime" be objectively verified via the defined audit procedure? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK013 - Are MSIX installability criteria measurable (exact gate command and expected artifact path)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK014 - Is smoke-checklist success defined as per-step pass/fail rather than a general impression? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 - Are requirements defined for the alternate flow where WindowsAppSDK 2.4.0 fails for SDK reasons? [Coverage, Alternate Flow, Research §spike]
- [ ] CHK016 - Are requirements defined for the exception flow where a kept package fails restore/build? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Research §R-05]
- [ ] CHK017 - Are detection requirements defined for source-generator behavior changes under the new compiler? [Coverage, Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK018 - Are offline-invariant requirements explicitly preserved through the migration (WAN-disabled suites as proof)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-002]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK019 - Is the constitution-amendment follow-up documented with an owner and timing, not just noted? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are structural assumptions (portable RIDs, warnings-as-errors off, Windows runner availability) validated rather than merely stated? [Assumption, Research §R-02/R-07]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit.implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit.specify` and `/speckit.clarify`
- Focus per reviewer: requirements quality only (Q1:A), standard depth (Q2:B), equal weight across pin precision, packaging/smoke, and baseline measurability (Q3:D)
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
